Skills pick whichever provider in a category is connected (see [Supported integrations](#supported-integrations)) 3. Run any premium skill — your AI now has direct access to your marketing data. On **Solo**, skills record what they find with `create_finding`. On **Cloud**, they use tickets (`create_ticket`) and can also use BigQuery, scripts, automations and image generation. Every skill handles both plans. ### Supported integrations Skills are written against jobs ("ad-level spend", "campaign report", "lost deals"), not one vendor. A skill runs on any connected provider in the category and reports each one separately when several are connected. | Category | Providers | |----------|-----------| | Paid search | Google Ads, Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads), Apple Search Ads, OpenAI Ads | | Paid social | Meta Ads, LinkedIn Ads, TikTok Ads, X Ads, Reddit Ads, Snapchat Ads, Bidtheatre | | B2B attribution | Fibbler | | Web & product analytics | Google Analytics 4, Plausible, Fathom Analytics, Simple Analytics, Adobe Analytics, Microsoft Clarity, PostHog, Mixpanel, Segment, AppsFlyer, GrowthBook | | Tagging | Google Tag Manager | | SEO & AI search | Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, Semrush, Ahrefs, AI Visibility (ChatGPT / Claude / Gemini / Perplexity), Brave Search | | Email | Klaviyo, Mailchimp, Rule, Get a Newsletter, Brevo, MailerLite, Drip, Braze, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Symplify | | CRM & forms | HubSpot, Pipedrive, Upsales, HubSpot Forms | | Organic social & community | LinkedIn Organic, X Organic, YouTube, Discord, Crisp | | Ecommerce | Shopify, WooCommerce, Abicart, Litium, ShipStation | | CMS | WordPress, Webflow, Ghost, Framer, Wix, Sanity, Contentful | | Billing & finance | Stripe, Fortnox | | Creative | Image generation (Cloud) | The routing rules every skill follows (tool names, plan differences, choosing a provider, same-job tables) are in [`skills/marketing-engineer/references/mcp-routing.md`](skills/marketing-engineer/references/mcp-routing.md). ## How It Works **Free skills** use `WebFetch` and `WebSearch` to analyze publicly available data. No accounts or API keys needed. **Premium skills** use [Cogny's MCP gateway](https://cogny.com), which federates 60+ integrations through the Cogny MCP proxy. Your AI runs locally (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, etc.), and Cogny holds the credentials and serves the data. ``` Your Claude Code ──MCP──> Cogny MCP gateway ──> Cogny MCP proxy ──OAuth/Token──> Google Ads / Meta / LinkedIn / TikTok / Reddit / … (local) app.cogny.com/mcp (hosted) GA4 / Search Console / Semrush / Ahrefs / … Klaviyo / Mailchimp / Brevo / HubSpot / Shopify / … (your accounts) ``` Every connected integration appears as `mcp____`, e.g. `mcp__Google_Ads__tool_execute_gaql`. With the server registered as `cogny` in `.mcp.json`, Claude Code shows that as `mcp__cogny__mcp__Google_Ads__tool_execute_gaql`, which is the form the skills use. Old names like `mcp__cogny__google_ads__…` are no longer served. ## Results ### GrowthHackers.se — +271% organic clicks in 3 weeks Connected Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools via Cogny MCP. Ran `/seo-audit` + `/seo-monitor` after a site migration. | Metric | Before | After | |--------|--------|-------| | Organic clicks | baseline | **+271%** | | Click-through rate | 0.29% | **0.66%** | | Search impressions | baseline | **+60%** | | AI citations (Bing Copilot) | baseline | **+154%** | | PageSpeed score | 78 | **97** | > "Cogny gave Claude Code eyes into our actual search data. > The audit caught things we'd never have found manually." > — Yi Li, CEO at GrowthHackers [Read the full case study →](https://cogny.com/case-studies/growthhackers-4x-organic-traffic) --- *Got results? [Open an issue](https://github.com/cognyai/claude-code-marketing-skills/issues) and we'll feature you here.* ## Contributing PRs welcome! See individual skill files for the format. Skills should include: - YAML frontmatter with metadata - Clear step-by-step instructions - Specific queries/actions (not vague recommendations) - Example output format - Read-only tools in `allowed-tools`. Write tools (pause, create, send, schedule) prompt the user. Tool names are checked against the real Cogny MCP surface: ```bash # Regenerate the catalog from the Cogny monorepo (services/mcp-proxy) python3 scripts/build-mcp-catalog.py ../cogny/services/mcp-proxy/src/servers # Check every mcp__cogny__… reference in skills/ python3 scripts/check-tool-names.py ``` ## License MIT

Setting up Premium Skills

1. Sign up at cogny.com

2. Connect the accounts you use. Skills pick whichever provider in a category is connected (see [Supported integrations](#supported-integrations))

3. Add Cogny to your .mcp.json:


{

  "mcpServers": {

    "cogny": {

      "type": "http",

      "url": "https://app.cogny.com/mcp"

    }

  }

}

4. Claude Code will open a browser for OAuth login on first use.

5. Run any premium skill — your AI now has direct access to your marketing data.

On Solo, skills record what they find with create_finding. On Cloud, they use tickets (create_ticket) and can also use BigQuery, scripts, automations and image generation. Every skill handles both plans.

How It Works

Free skills use WebFetch and WebSearch to analyze publicly available data. No accounts or API keys needed.

Premium skills use Cogny's MCP gateway, which federates 60+ integrations through the Cogny MCP proxy. Your AI runs locally (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, etc.), and Cogny holds the credentials and serves the data.


Your Claude Code ──MCP──> Cogny MCP gateway ──> Cogny MCP proxy ──OAuth/Token──> Google Ads / Meta / LinkedIn / TikTok / Reddit / …

    (local)               app.cogny.com/mcp     (hosted)                         GA4 / Search Console / Semrush / Ahrefs / …

                                                                                 Klaviyo / Mailchimp / Brevo / HubSpot / Shopify / …

                                                                                 (your accounts)

Every connected integration appears as mcp__<Integration>__<tool>, e.g. mcp__Google_Ads__tool_execute_gaql. With the server registered as cogny in .mcp.json, Claude Code shows that as mcp__cogny__mcp__Google_Ads__tool_execute_gaql, which is the form the skills use. Old names like mcp__cogny__google_ads__… are no longer served. <!-- check-tool-names: ignore -->

Contributing

PRs welcome! See individual skill files for the format. Skills should include:

  • YAML frontmatter with metadata
  • Clear step-by-step instructions
  • Specific queries/actions (not vague recommendations)
  • Example output format
  • Read-only tools in allowed-tools. Write tools (pause, create, send, schedule) prompt the user.

Tool names are checked against the real Cogny MCP surface:


# Regenerate the catalog from the Cogny monorepo (services/mcp-proxy)

python3 scripts/build-mcp-catalog.py ../cogny/services/mcp-proxy/src/servers



# Check every mcp__cogny__… reference in skills/

python3 scripts/check-tool-names.py
